messages:
jonathan: Heads-up — got an enterprise escalation from AcmeCorp citing p95/p99 spikes starting ~18:40 UTC after the midnight rollout. They see tails go from ~220ms to >1.2s for text-generation requests. cc @maya @renee :eyes:

maya: on it. any recent runtime deploys?

jonathan: small cache change landed in canary earlier today: PR #4128 (kv prefix key normalizer) + eviction tweak. deploy-bot: `deploy/runtime-canary v1.12.3 -> production` showed green at 18:05.

renee: pulling traces now. initial look — a bunch of requests show cache-miss waterfall on KV prefix cache. Miss ratio jumped from 8% -> 48% on the affected nodes right around 18:10. p99 tokens spent waiting on KV reads.

devon: I saw similar in internal load tests earlier — the normalizer truncated keys to 64 bytes (intended) but it looks like we changed to `substr(0,64)` instead of hashing after normalization. That increases collision risk and causes eviction churn for hot prefixes.

laura: logs from node-17:```
2026-03-14T18:12:07Z WARN cache miss prefix_key=7f4a2b... hits=0
2026-03-14T18:12:07Z INFO evicting key=7f4a2b... size=1024
2026-03-14T18:12:07Z INFO insert key=9f3d11... size=1100
2026-03-14T18:12:08Z WARN cache miss prefix_key=7f4a2b...
```

laura: you can see churn — same logical prefix mapping to many different physical keys. eviction rate jumps correlate with P99.

maya: is this the `prefix_key` generation wrinkle we've discussed? the normalizer used to produce SHA256(normalized) but PR used truncated substring for readability in logs then accidentally left in production.

jonathan: that matches. PR diff excerpt:```
- const key = sha256(normalized)
+ const key = normalized.slice(0,64)
```

devon: oof. that explains both higher miss rate and higher eviction rate because our LRU/size buckets now treat collisions as distinct keys; plus some keys exceed bucket sizing causing repeated evictions -> thrash.

renee: mitigation plan proposals:
1) Quick rollback of PR #4128 to restore sha256-based keys (hotfix) — low-risk, small blast radius.
2) If rollback delayed: increase prefix-cache capacity on affected nodes by +50% and temporarily adjust eviction to keep longer TTL for keys with >X hits.
3) Add short-term request-side throttle for known noisy tenants (AcmeCorp) to reduce burst concurrency while we fix.

maya: prepare rollback, but also we should gather repro steps and a minimal test that demonstrates miss ratio regression. I can draft the rollback PR and hotfix patch.

jonathan: @oncall-bot please page infra-oncall for rolling restart of canary nodes after rollback.

oncall-bot: paging infra-oncall... (triggered by jonathan)

devon: repro steps I used in staging — load script below. reproduces miss spike within ~5 minutes:```
# repro.sh (run on staging with 200 concurrent clients)
for i in $(seq 1 100000); do
  curl -sS -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" \
    -d '{"model":"open-kvm-1","prompt":"summary: Very long prompt text ..."}' &
done
wait
```

laura: metrics to watch: prefix_cache_miss_ratio, prefix_cache_evictions, prefix_cache_inserts, gc_pause_ms, runtime_request_latency_p99. dashboards created: /dashboards/prefix-cache-regen.

maya: rollback PR posted: https://git.redwood/infra/runtime/pull/4172 (reverts #4128). Patch also adds a unit test for `makePrefixKey()` covering unicode and long inputs.

jonathan: rolling that now. canary nodes will pick up in ~2 min. after deploy we should see miss ratio drop to baseline.

cache-bot: canary-deploy runtime v1.12.4 (rollback) started @ 18:28 UTC on nodes: node-17,node-18,node-19

laura: node-17 metrics already showing decreased eviction rate, miss ratio trending down from 48% -> 12% at 18:34. p99 latency trending down on AcmeCorp from ~1.2s -> 270ms.

renee: leaving monitoring up. if we still see tail we may need capacity bump; but rollback looks like primary fix.

devon: follow-ups:
- Add a pre-merge test in CI that runs `prefix_key_collision_test` under random unicode inputs.
- Change key generation to: `sha256(normalized + tenant_id)` to avoid cross-tenant collisions.
- Add metric `prefix_key_entropy` to detect low-entropy key distributions.
- Consider switching eviction to segmented LRU (hot vs cold priors) to reduce thrash.

maya: PR #4180 filed for improvements + tests. Also added escalation notes and timeline for postmortem.

jonathan: customer update draft: "we identified a cache key regression introduced during a canary change. We rolled back the change and observed p99 return to expected levels. We'll follow up with a permanent fix and tests. Apologies for the disruption." anyone want to edit?

laura: looks good, add ETA for follow-up fix (48 hours) and mention we've throttled bursts for them while we validate.

jonathan: sent to AcmeCorp. Support ticket updated and SRE runbook entry created: `/runbooks/prefix-cache-troubleshooting`.

renee: closing the immediate incident but keeping this thread open for postmortem notes. I'll start a postmortem template and link metrics + traces.

maya: small note — we should also check the warmup path. because of collisions some commonly-used prefixes were evicted before they warmed up under burst. add warmup pin for known-hot prefixes in next iteration.

devon: agreed. I'll prototype segmented LRU and a small in-memory bloom filter to prevent accidental double-inserts during heavy churn.

laura: thanks all. summary: root cause — bad key normalization change introduced substring-based keys -> collisions and eviction thrash -> p95/p99 regressions. mitigation — rollback PR #4172 applied, metrics normalized. follow-ups — tests, sha256 + tenant_id, segmented LRU, warmup pins.

jonathan: archival note: filing incident reference INC-2026-0314-cache-thrash.

cache-bot: incident closed (auto) — root cause identified, rollback applied, follow-up tasks created. :white_check_mark:
